title: ANNEX — TRANSLATION SECTION
summary: The annex contains two extended song cycles. “You and I” follows the eighteen-parva arc of the Mahābhārata in compressed poetic episodes, while “The Unborn Mind” unfolds across twenty-eight cantos as a separate philosophical-lyric sequence. Both retain internal sequential navigation rather than being flattened into the book’s ordinary poem list.

entries.title: Annex 1 — You and I (Song Cycle)
entries.summary: An extended sequence in 18 internal parts, centred on earth & natural imagery, society & power and body & consciousness. Its subordinate poems or cantos develop the parent title through successive shifts of image, argument and voice.

entries.title: Adi Parva
entries.summary: The cycle opens by addressing Vyāsa and the making of the Bhārata itself, then moves through the dynastic origins and rivalries that shape the Kuru world. It follows the emergence of the Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī’s marriage, conflict with the Kauravas and the burning of the Khāṇḍava forest, ending with Maya’s promise to build an unmatched assembly hall.

entries.title: Sabha Parva
entries.summary: Maya’s assembly hall becomes the setting for Yudhiṣṭhira’s Rājasūya ambitions, the defeat of Jarāsandha and a display of imperial power. The movement then darkens into envy, the dice games, Draupadī’s humiliation and the second loss that condemns the Pāṇḍavas to twelve years of forest exile and a year in concealment.

entries.title: Vana Parva
entries.summary: The Pāṇḍavas enter forest exile with Draupadī and Dhaumya, while stories, encounters and tests repeatedly turn hardship into ethical inquiry. The parva culminates in the Yakṣa’s questions, where Yudhiṣṭhira’s refusal to favour one maternal line over another becomes the reason all his brothers are restored.

entries.title: Virata Parva
entries.summary: With twelve years of exile complete, the Pāṇḍavas live incognito in Virāṭa’s court under assumed roles. The sequence includes Kīcaka’s pursuit of Draupadī, the recovery of stolen cattle and Arjuna’s return to arms, before concealed identities are revealed and Uttara is married to Abhimanyu.

entries.title: Udyoga Parva
entries.summary: Marriage celebrations give way to diplomacy and preparation for war. Alliances form, Krishna offers a choice between his unarmed presence and his army, peace efforts fail, and the opposing forces gather at Kurukṣetra under Bhīṣma and Dhṛṣṭadyumna while Sañjaya receives the power to narrate the coming battle.

entries.title: Bhishma Parva
entries.summary: The war begins with Arjuna’s crisis before his own kin and Krishna’s teaching on action, attachment and the deathless self. Fighting then advances through the first ten days until Śikhaṇḍī and Arjuna bring Bhīṣma down onto the bed of arrows, where he postpones death and speaks with Karṇa.

entries.title: Drona Parva
entries.summary: Drona becomes Kaurava commander and the battle grows increasingly strategic and destructive. Arjuna is drawn away, Abhimanyu is trapped and killed, Jayadratha falls, and the parva ends with the deceptive announcement of Aśvatthāma’s death that causes Drona to lay down his weapons and be killed by Dhṛṣṭadyumna.

entries.title: Karna Parva
entries.summary: Karṇa assumes command and the struggle narrows toward his long-awaited confrontation with Arjuna. After sparing Nakula in keeping with his promise to Kuntī, Karṇa fights under Śalya’s charioteering; when his chariot wheel sinks, Arjuna rejects his appeal to battlefield dharma and kills him.

entries.title: Shalya Parva
entries.summary: Śalya’s command ends when Yudhiṣṭhira kills him, while Sahadeva kills Śakuni and Ulūka. Duryodhana hides in a lake but is drawn into a mace duel with Bhīma, who fulfils his vow by breaking Duryodhana’s thigh, bringing the open battle close to its end.

entries.title: Sauptika Parva
entries.summary: Aśvatthāma responds to Duryodhana’s defeat with a night attack on the sleeping Pāṇḍava camp. Ignoring Kripa’s warning that such action is adharma, he kills Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Śikhaṇḍī and Draupadī’s sons, burns the camp and carries the war beyond the recognised limits of battle.

entries.title: Stri Parva
entries.summary: The women and elders confront the human cost of the war. Dhṛtarāṣṭra’s grief and anger, Gandhārī’s lament and curse upon Krishna, and the cremation of the dead turn victory into mourning and close one side of the conflict with bereavement rather than triumph.

entries.title: Shanti Parva
entries.summary: Yudhiṣṭhira, shattered by the war, wants to renounce rule, but Vyāsa turns him back toward responsibility. After his coronation he approaches Bhīṣma for instruction in kingship, social duty, liberation and care for subjects.

entries.title: Anushasana Parva
entries.summary: As the sun turns northward, Yudhiṣṭhira and the family return to Bhīṣma. After fifty-eight days on the bed of arrows, Bhīṣma gives his final teaching, dies and is cremated amid collective grief.

entries.title: Ashvamedhika Parva
entries.summary: Hastināpura returns to prosperity, and Krishna revives Uttara’s lifeless child, Parīkṣit, by invoking the integrity of his own conduct. Yudhiṣṭhira then performs the Aśvamedha; the roaming horse returns without successful challenge and the sacrifice is completed.

entries.title: Ashramavasika Parva
entries.summary: Fifteen years later, Dhṛtarāṣṭra withdraws to the forest with Gandhārī, Kuntī, Vidura and Sañjaya. Vidura enters samādhi, and a forest fire finally takes the lives of those who remain in retirement.

entries.title: Mausala Parva
entries.summary: The Yādavas destroy one another in internal violence after insulting learned men. Balarāma enters samādhi, Krishna is fatally struck in the foot by the hunter Jarā, and Vāsudeva dies after hearing of Krishna’s death.

entries.title: Mahaprasthanika Parva
entries.summary: After Krishna’s death, Yudhiṣṭhira gives the kingdom to Parīkṣit and the Pāṇḍavas begin their final Himalayan journey with Draupadī and a dog. One companion after another falls; Yudhiṣṭhira refuses Indra’s heaven without the dog, who is then revealed as Yama testing his fidelity.

entries.title: Svargarohana Parva
entries.summary: Yudhiṣṭhira reaches heaven but refuses to remain there when he is shown Draupadī and his brothers in hell. Yama reveals this as a third test, after the Yakṣa and the dog; Yudhiṣṭhira passes, receives a divine form, and the cycle closes by turning the ancient quarrel of ‘you and I’ into a warning against enduring attachment and division.

entries.title: Annex 2 — The Unborn Mind (Song Cycle)
entries.summary: An extended sequence in 28 internal parts, centred on earth & natural imagery, body & consciousness and society & power. Its subordinate poems or cantos develop the parent title through successive shifts of image, argument and voice.

entries.title: Canto 1
entries.summary: A meditation on earth & natural imagery, society & power and suffering & fear. The recurring register of body and breath helps carry the poem’s movement.

entries.title: Canto 2
entries.summary: A meditation on time & impermanence, body & consciousness and language & meaning. It moves from time & impermanence toward body & consciousness, allowing the poem’s emphasis to change as it develops.
